message: Command `cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/proj.4 && grep -rn "PJD_ERR\|#define.*ERR\|set_errno" src/projects.h src/proj.h src/*.h 2>/dev/null | grep -i "err" | head -40` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
The `CHECK_RETURN` macro uses `transient_error[-defn->ctx->last_errno]`. Here `last_errno` could be negative (error codes are negative like -14). If `last_errno` is negative, `-last_errno` is positive. If `last_errno` is, say, -50 or less, then `-last_errno` >= 50, which is out of bounds for the 50-element `transient_error` array! 

The condition is `defn->ctx->last_errno > 0 || transient_error[-defn->ctx->last_errno] == 0`. If `last_errno` is negative and less than -49 (i.e., -50 or more negative), then `-last_errno` >= 50, causing an out-of-bounds read of `transient_error`.

But wait - in the fuzzer, `point_count == 1`. Let me check: in `pj_transform`, the `transient_error[-last_errno]` is guarded by `point_count == 1` short-circuit. But in `pj_datum_transform`, the `CHECK_RETURN` macro does NOT have the `point_count == 1` guard! Let me re-read:

```c
#define CHECK_RETURN(defn) {if( defn->ctx->last_errno != 0 && (defn->ctx->last_errno > 0 || transient_error[-defn->ctx->last_errno] == 0) ) { if( z_is_temp ) pj_dalloc(z); return defn->ctx->last_errno; }}
```

So if `last_errno` is negative and `-last_errno` >= 50, this reads out of bounds. But we need `last_errno` to be a specific negative value. The error codes in proj are typically in range -1 to -44. Let me check what error codes can be set. Let me look at `pj_strerrno.c` or the error definitions.

Actually, let me reconsider. The issue says "array lookup with wrong indices due to missing validation before accessing the array". The `transient_error[-last_errno]` is exactly an array lookup with an index derived from `last_errno` without validation that `-last_errno` is within [0, 49]. This matches the issue description perfectly!

But we need `last_errno` to be a value that makes `-last_errno` out of bounds. The error codes are negative. Let me check what values `last_errno` can take. Let me look at the error code definitions.
